title: JavaScript Operators and Expressions knowledge check

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of a precise TypeScript type?
options: To express the intended values and let the compiler detect incompatible uses.
To convert or sanitize an external value at runtime.
questions.answer_key: To express the intended values and let the compiler detect incompatible uses.
questions.explanation: Types describe expected program values but do not automatically change or validate runtime data.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct about “JavaScript Operators and Expressions”?
options: The concept should be demonstrated with arithmetic and comparison and checked against its intended contract.
The safest approach is to skip diagnostics and trust the first output.
A type assertion automatically validates every value at runtime.
The learner should publish hidden solutions so the exercise can grade itself.
questions.answer_key: The concept should be demonstrated with arithmetic and comparison and checked against its intended contract.
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus explicitly includes “Arithmetic and comparison”; connect it to a concrete example and verify the behavior relevant to this lesson.

questions.prompt: What is a good verification step after practicing “JavaScript Operators and Expressions”?
options: Assume assignment and conditional expressions is unnecessary because the code has type annotations.
Ignore compiler or test failures if the interface looks correct.
Treat passing a static token check as proof that the program executed correctly.
Check logical and nullish operators, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.answer_key: Check logical and nullish operators, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.explanation: The syllabus includes “Logical and nullish operators”. Verification should match the concept: type-level checks, runtime tests, configuration checks or human review as appropriate.
